name: Close
summary: Sales CRM unifying calling, email and SMS in one inbox, for teams that live on the phone.
best_for: inside-sales teams that live on the phone and want calling, SMS and CRM in one place
skip_if: your sales are mostly email or self-serve — a cheaper CRM without built-in calling covers you
honest_knock: The built-in calling is the draw, but call and SMS credits stack on top of the seat price — a '$99' plan can effectively cost ~$160/user once a rep dials 50+ times a day. Great for call-heavy teams, pricey if you barely dial.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Solo, per user · per month, billed month to month
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-19 on close.com/pricing and close.com/pricing.md, unchanged) Per-seat: Solo $19, Essentials $49, Growth $109 and Scale $149 per user/mo, or $9, $35, $99 and $139 billed annually — the same twelve amounts we have now read on 23 July, 3, 11 and 14 August, 12 September and 19 October 2026. No free plan; the trial runs 14 days and close.com states no credit card is required, with $5 of calling and enrichment credits included, and the page carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. AI credits are pooled per tier (500 a month on Solo, then 1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 per user up to 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000). Chloe, the AI sales agent Close now leads the page with, is free to access on every plan but spends those AI credits plus telephony as she works, so she is metered rather than included. Call minutes, SMS and dialer credits are billed separately and can meaningfully raise the real cost: outbound calls run about $0.02 a minute and phone lines start at about $1 a month. The Call Assistant add-on is $50 a month per organisation plus $0.02 a minute, and additional organisations are $50 a month each, with Growth and Scale including one free secondary org. Premium Phone Numbers are listed as a feature with no price attached.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 during the trial, without a card, without setting up a phone number or connecting email, and without sending anything: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported a CSV with four rows (one made-up company with two contacts and two companies with one), compared the result with the file, and exported the leads as CSV and JSON.
findings: The trial does not start without consent to sales calls and texts. The last sign-up screen asks for a phone number with a box 'By providing your phone number, you agree to receive calls and texts from Close, including automated messages and calls using AI-powered agents'; without ticking it, sign-up stops at 'You must agree to receive communications'. No card was asked, and the app then showed 'Subscribe · 14d left' on day one.

With the default import options, our four rows became 4 leads instead of 3: the company with two contacts appeared twice, once per contact, even though 'Check if Lead already exists' (on lead name) was on. Merging rows per company needs 'Group related rows', which is off by default and which we left off. Statuses and our TestID field arrived correctly per lead.

Five of six columns were matched automatically. For our TestID column we added a custom field, and in that window 'Enable enrichment' is on by default ('the AI will attempt to fill the field'); we switched it off before saving.

Export offers leads, contacts or opportunities, CSV or JSON, and current-view, common or all fields, but 'A link to the generated file will be emailed to you.' Both exports arrived by email within about 10 seconds, and the download link requires logging in. The CSV had 4 rows and 274 columns with primary-contact columns per lead; the JSON had a contacts list per lead. Each lead held one contact in our import, so we could not check whether extra contacts would be lost in the CSV.
The export split the contact name 'AIBM-001 Contact A' into first name 'AIBM-001' and last name 'A', dropping 'Contact'; the full name was still in primary_contact_name.
Import takes CSV only (up to 15 MB), next to copy-paste, import from another CRM or from email. The trial screen also offered a live demo and a $5 calling credit for setting up a phone number.
not_tested: Calling, SMS, email sequences and AI enrichment
The trial's credits and what uses them
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
